hints.title: Values are also positions
hints.body: Every value is a valid index because it lies between 1 and `n`, and the list has indices 0 through `n`. Treat `nums[i]` as the next position to visit from position `i`.

hints.title: The graph has a cycle
hints.body: The mapping `i -> nums[i]` forms a functional graph. Because a value is repeated, two different positions point to the same place, which creates a cycle that can be detected without extra memory.

hints.title: Find the cycle entrance
hints.body: Use one slow and one fast pointer to meet inside the cycle. Then reset one pointer to the start and advance both one step at a time; they meet at the entrance, which is the repeated value.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
slow = nums[0]
fast = nums[0]
repeat:
    slow = nums[slow]
    fast = nums[nums[fast]]
until slow == fast
slow = nums[0]
while slow != fast:
    slow = nums[slow]
    fast = nums[fast]
return slow
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution.
